entries.title: Ezekiel 3:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Eat - This was done in a vision. Findeth - In the hand which was sent to him.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Belly - The mouth is the proper instrument of eating, but when meat is digested, the belly is said to eat. Fill thy bowels - This denotes the fulness of the measure wherewith we should read, meditate, and digest the word of God. Honey - It was sweet to receive things by revelation from God, and so to converse with God. And usually the first part of the ministerial work is pleasant.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Speak - What things I shall shew thee, and in what words I shall declare them to thee.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Many people - Divers nations, that thou shouldest need divers tongues, to speak to them all in their own language.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: All - The far greater part, tho' not every particular person.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I have - I have given thee, constancy, and manly carriage. The more impudent wicked people are in their opposition to religion, the more openly and resolutely should God's people appear in the practice and defence of it.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Captivity - Of the first captivity under Jeconiah's reign, who succeeded his father Jehoiakim, slain for his conspiracy with Egypt against Nebuchadnezzar.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A voice - An articulate sound, of many angels, attended with the rushing of the wheels, added to the noise of their wings. Blessed - Praised be the gloriously holy and just God. His place - Coming down from heaven.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rushing - The wheels of providence moved over against the angels, and in concert with them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Spirit - Caught him up into the air. Took - Carried me to the place where the captive Jews were crowded together. Bitterness - Not at all pleased with my work. He went in the heat of his spirit; because of the discouragements he foresaw he should meet with. But the hand of the Lord was strong upon him, not only to compel him to the work, but to fit him for it.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Tel - abib - A part of Mesopotamia, which was shut up within Chebar westward, and Saocora eastward. By - On that part of the river Chebar, which runs west - ward of Tel - abib. Where - Where I found them sitting astonished, at the sight of their change from freedom and honour to servitude and shame. Seven days - Mourning no doubt all that while, and waiting 'till the spirit of prophecy should open his mouth.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I Lay - Permit it to be laid before him. He shall - Perish in his sin. Remembered - Shall not be profitable to him; "he that apostatizes is the worst of men, because he falls from known ways of goodness and holiness."

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: There - At Tel - abib. Go forth - Withdraw from the multitude.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: As the glory - We are not now to expect such visions. But we have a favour done us nothing inferior, if we by faith behold the glory of the Lord, so as to be changed into the same image. And this honour have all his saints.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shut - To foresignify the shutting up of the Jews in Jerusalem.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Not go - Thou shalt be straitly confined.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: But - When ever I shall reveal any thing to thee. Open - I will give thee power to speak. Let - 'Tis his duty and safety. Forbear - 'Tis at his own peril.
